state.context: One Canlang token, require, presently serves several roles. Its Given declaration, require Model: predicate, defines a side-effect-free rule over row, enforced for affected final-state records on all mutation routes with relevant dependency rechecks; preference values can likewise be constrained. In When, require expr [message=expr] appears ahead of do or among its statements, follows source order, and on failure returns a safe rule_failed business error while discarding all tentative work, trusted execution included. A Then require expr controls its surrounding render scope: false excludes a group or denies a page, without overriding backend authorization. Backfill mappers also contain execution checks. The author is exploring asserts for one side of the Given versus When/Then divide and rules out renaming both sides; no source alteration was requested. Rust assert! fails by panic and supports testing/runtime invariants. TypeScript uses asserts in assertion signatures for flow-sensitive type refinement. Those associations offer recognition but do not specify Canlang outcomes. All replacement words are hypothetical and must keep behavior identical.
state.aim: Weigh recognition, distinction between enduring data rules and immediate conditions, expected rejection/visibility behavior, vocabulary size, and costs of updating draft source, parser and highlighting. A single shared word remains a valid possibility, and Canlang need not inherit panic semantics.

spelling.instructions: Select the naming arrangement with the strongest overall fit to these facts. Balance advantages and disadvantages of each proposal; the classification conveys a recommendation and cannot authorize a migration.

criteria.keep: Continue using require in each location. Avoids extra terminology and migration while emphasizing shared condition enforcement; the section and colon still carry the difference between state rules, operation guards and presentation eligibility.
criteria.given_asserts: Rename only Given constraints to asserts Model: predicate, keeping require for operations, UI and maintenance checks. The new token highlights declarative enforcement and recalls assertions; its extra vocabulary may also evoke individual test assertions or failure conventions.
criteria.when_then_asserts: Reserve require for Given and write asserts in When, Then and matching backfill guard positions. Recognition of a checking verb can distinguish immediate checks from state declarations; ordinary rejection and omitted UI can clash with assertion expectations, and sources/tools need a new word.
criteria.given_invariant: Spell only the Given rule invariant Model: predicate and leave require in scenarios, rendering and backfill. Its name explicitly expresses a durable constraint rather than a local guard; the term is longer and more specialized, with consequent draft/parser/editor updates.
